skill.name: code-review-playbook
skill.description: Use this skill to run structured code reviews with checklists, conventional comments, review templates, and guidance for reviewers and authors.
skill.summary: A practical playbook for consistent pull request reviews, self-reviews, security checks, and constructive feedback.
skill.author: AI Agent Hub

security_audit.summary: All 64 static hits are false positives from Markdown examples, inline code, review language, or a documentation link. Semantic findings cover external AI API submission of source code and prompt construction without untrusted-input guardrails.

remediation.issue: External AI API examples can disclose private code.
remediation.suggestion: Require user consent, redaction, and approved data handling before sending PR diffs, codebase context, or source code to external model APIs.

remediation.issue: Prompt examples treat reviewed code as normal prompt text.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to delimit reviewed code and state that code comments, diffs, and file contents are untrusted data.

remediation.issue: Advanced API examples lack operational guardrails.
remediation.suggestion: Mark SDK examples as optional and require confirmation before any agent performs network calls or uses external services.

semantic_findings.title: External AI API Submission of Source Code
semantic_findings.description: The playbook examples send PR diffs, codebase context, and raw code through the Anthropic SDK. This can disclose private source code without consent or redaction.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples construct API requests containing prDiff, codebaseContext, and code values. They are documentation examples, so the risk depends on users following them.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Review Input Used Without Prompt Guardrails
semantic_findings.description: The advanced review prompts interpolate diffs and code directly into model instructions. Malicious code comments could influence the review unless the input is treated as data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The prompts include raw PR and code content inside instruction text, and no nearby guidance defines those contents as untrusted. The issue is contextual rather than executable.

content.user_title: Improve Code Reviews With a Structured Playbook
content.value_statement: Inconsistent reviews miss defects and create unclear feedback for authors. This skill provides checklists, comment formats, and templates for reliable pull request reviews.
actual_capabilities: Guides reviewers through pre-review, high-level review, detailed review, testing, and documentation checks.
Provides conventional comment labels for praise, issues, questions, security concerns, bugs, and blocking feedback.
Includes checklists for correctness, maintainability, testing, performance, API design, database changes, and security.
Supplies PR and security review templates for consistent feedback and self-review.
Explains review metrics, anti-patterns, and escalation patterns for team review processes.
limitations: Does not inspect a repository automatically or replace human judgment.
Does not run tests, linters, dependency scanners, or security tools by itself.
Examples that use external AI APIs require privacy review before use with private code.
Language guidance is broad and may need adaptation for specific frameworks.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Apply a consistent checklist before approving, commenting, or requesting changes on a pull request.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Self-Review
use_cases.description: Check scope, tests, documentation, and risk areas before asking teammates for review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Feedback
use_cases.description: Create shared comment labels, review expectations, and quality gates for a team.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic PR Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-review-playbook to review this pull request. Focus on correctness, tests, readability, and clear conventional comments.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare My Self-Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the playbook as a self-review checklist. Identify missing tests, unclear code, documentation gaps, and risks before I request review.

prompt_templates.title: Review Security-Sensitive Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the security review sections to assess authentication, authorization, input validation, secrets handling, logging, and rate limiting in this change.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Team Review Standard
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the playbook to create a team review process with comment labels, approval criteria, review metrics, and escalation rules.

output_examples.input: Review request for a medium pull request with new API behavior.
output: issue [blocking]: Add authorization checks before returning account data.
suggestion [non-blocking]: Split the validation logic into a named helper.
praise: The new tests cover the main success path clearly.

output_examples.input: Self-review before opening a pull request.
output: Scope is focused and tied to the linked ticket.
Tests cover the success path, but error handling still needs coverage.
Documentation should mention the changed response behavior.

output_examples.input: Team process update for review quality.
output: Use security and bug labels as blocking by default.
Keep pull requests under 400 lines when practical.
Track review time and follow-up rounds each sprint.

best_practices: Read the pull request goal before commenting on individual lines.
Separate blocking defects from optional preferences with conventional comments.
Ask for privacy approval before sending private code to external AI services.
anti_patterns: Approving large changes without reading the full context.
Blocking merges over personal style preferences handled by formatters.
Pasting private code into external review tools without team approval.

faq.question: Does this skill review code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a structured process and templates for an AI agent or human reviewer to apply.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is text-based and compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it include security review guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes checks for authentication, authorization, input validation, secrets, encryption, logging, and dependencies.

faq.question: Will it run tests or scanners?
faq.answer: No. Run tests, linters, and security scanners separately, then include results in the review context.

faq.question: Is it suitable for team standards?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes comment labels, PR templates, review metrics, and anti-patterns for team alignment.

faq.question: How should private code be handled?
faq.answer: Do not send private code to external services unless your team has approved the data handling requirements.
